description:
KAS VITALIS is an AI-powered astronaut health monitoring platform designed to support astronaut safety during space missions. It helps monitor vital signs, track physical and mental well-being, detect potential health risks, and provide timely alerts to support informed medical decisions. Our mission is to make space exploration safer through intelligent health insights and real-time monitoring.

Keeping Humanity Healthy Beyond Earth.
summary:
KAS VITALIS – Project Summary
KAS VITALIS is an AI-assisted astronaut health monitoring and mission management prototype designed for a hypothetical 900-day Mars mission. It integrates physiological monitoring, medical assessments, exercise tracking and mission resource management into one platform.

The system includes blood testing, urine analysis, ultrasound assessments, 12-lead ECG monitoring, muscle strength evaluation, nutrition tracking, wellbeing assessments and medical inventory management. It compares selected health measurements with preflight baselines to identify physiological changes during spaceflight.

Two AI models are integrated:
- MediaPipe Pose Landmarker: Tracks body movements and counts exercise repetitions using computer vision.
- BloodMNIST-trained MLP: Classifies microscopic blood-cell images, achieving 91.73% reported test accuracy.
Datasets: BloodMNIST supports blood-cell classification, while NASA OSD-942 provides research metadata related to bed-rest and exercise studies. Synthetic mission data supports demonstrations.

Technology: Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Cloudflare D1 and locally executed AI models.

Overall Objective: To provide a centralised platform for monitoring astronaut health, evaluating exercise performance, tracking physiological changes and supporting mission planning.
details:
KAS VITALIS — AI-Powered Astronaut Health and Mission Resource Monitoring System

Project Details

KAS VITALIS is an AI-assisted astronaut health monitoring and mission resource management platform designed to support human health, safety and well-being during long-duration space missions, particularly future expeditions to Mars.

Our project addresses one of the major challenges of deep-space exploration: maintaining astronaut health when medical resources are limited, physiological conditions are constantly changing and communication with Earth may be significantly delayed.

What Does Our Project Do?

KAS VITALIS integrates multiple health-monitoring and resource-management functions into a unified web application, demonstrated through a simulated 900-day Mars mission.

The system includes the following capabilities:

  • Comprehensive Health Monitoring: Tracks physiological parameters, including cardiovascular indicators, sleep, hydration and individual health trends, allowing astronauts to review changes against their preflight baselines.
  • AI-Powered Exercise Monitoring: Uses computer vision and Google's MediaPipe Pose Landmarker to identify body movements, measure joint angles, count repetitions and monitor exercise performance.
  • Blood Biomarker Analysis: Records and analyses laboratory-measured biomarkers, including bone turnover markers (CTX-1 and P1NP), vitamin D, iron, electrolytes, glucose, blood gases and selected cardiac biomarkers.
  • AI-Assisted Blood Cell Image Classification: Incorporates a machine-learning model trained using BloodMNIST to demonstrate automated classification of blood cell images. This experimental feature is distinct from laboratory blood biomarker measurement.
  • Advanced Medical Monitoring: Supports urine analysis, ECG measurements, ultrasound examination records, muscle strength assessment and tendon-related measurements.
  • Nutrition and Food Management: Tracks daily nutritional intake, available food inventory, meal consumption and projected food availability throughout the mission.
  • Mission Resource Management: Maintains records of essential equipment, medical supplies and mission consumables to support resource planning.
  • Health Trends and Decision Support: Uses baseline comparisons, rule-based calculations and visualisations to identify potentially concerning changes and provide understandable monitoring information.

How Does It Work?

Astronauts interact with KAS VITALIS through a central dashboard that consolidates their medical information, physical activity, nutritional records and mission resources.

The system processes manually entered measurements, imported laboratory results, exercise videos and simulated mission data.

Computer vision analyses exercise movements locally, while the health analysis modules calculate physiological trends and compare measurements with recorded baselines.

Mission resource functions track consumption and estimate remaining supplies. This enables astronauts to consider their health requirements alongside the resources available to support them.

The prototype is designed around local processing and data storage, reducing dependence on continuous communication with Earth.

Technologies and Tools Used

KAS VITALIS incorporates the following technologies:

  • Next.js, React and TypeScript: Web application development and interactive interfaces.
  • Tailwind CSS: Responsive dashboard design.
  • Google MediaPipe Pose Landmarker: Computer-vision-based exercise monitoring.
  • BloodMNIST and a Multilayer Perceptron (MLP): Experimental blood cell image classification.
  • JavaScript-based calculations: Health trends, biomarker comparisons, ECG-related calculations and resource estimates.
  • Cloudflare D1: Configured database persistence for application records.
  • Browser-based local storage: Local simulation data and supporting offline functionality.
  • NASA Open Science Data Repository: Scientific reference material relevant to spaceflight research.

The demonstration primarily uses synthetic astronaut and mission data. It does not rely on live spacecraft medical feeds or real-time NASA astronaut health records.

What Makes KAS VITALIS Innovative?

The main innovation of KAS VITALIS is its integration of astronaut health intelligence with mission resource management.

Traditional health-monitoring applications primarily focus on individual physiological indicators. KAS VITALIS connects medical measurements, exercise performance, nutritional intake and available mission supplies within one environment.

Its computer vision features provide a practical approach to monitoring movement, while personalised baseline comparisons support longitudinal health analysis.

The inclusion of experimental blood cell classification, ECG analysis, ultrasound records, bone biomarkers and muscle performance measurements expands the scope beyond basic wearable health tracking.

Rather than focusing on a single medical parameter, KAS VITALIS offers a multidisciplinary approach to astronaut health monitoring.

Benefits and Intended Impact

KAS VITALIS aims to:

  • Improve astronauts' awareness of their physical and physiological health.
  • Support earlier recognition of potentially concerning health trends.
  • Encourage consistent exercise and nutrition monitoring.
  • Improve visibility of food, equipment and medical supplies.
  • Reduce dependence on continuous Earth-based monitoring.
  • Support informed decisions during prolonged communication delays.
  • Provide a foundation for future research into autonomous astronaut health-support systems.

The long-term vision is to help future space crews maintain their health and operational readiness throughout extended missions to the Moon, Mars and beyond.

Important Design Considerations

During development, our team considered the effects of microgravity, radiation, cardiovascular adaptation, musculoskeletal deterioration, nutritional limitations, communication delays and restricted medical resources.

We also prioritised data accessibility, personalised monitoring, explainable calculations and the ability to operate with limited connectivity.

KAS VITALIS is currently a research and hackathon prototype, not a clinically validated medical device. Its AI outputs and monitoring alerts are intended to demonstrate decision-support capabilities, not provide autonomous medical diagnoses or treatment.

Our Vision

KAS VITALIS aims to transform astronaut health monitoring from isolated measurements into an integrated, intelligent and resource-aware system that supports human health during the next era of deep-space exploration.

Monitor Health. Optimise Resources. Sustain Life Beyond Earth.
